title: sync-retry-presets-and-introduce-pull-generator-stream-facade-across-py-ts-go
author: Mira Chen
release_notes: Aligned retry preset names and defaults across Python/TS/Go SDKs; introduce lightweight PullGenerator streaming facade for ergonomic pull-based consumption; minor SDK patch bumps (py 1.12.3, ts 2.7.1, go 0.9.8); telemetry hooks for retry events.
description:
Context and motivation: The three SDKs diverged subtly in retry semantics and streaming ergonomics after the recent session/lease work. Downstream teams saw inconsistent behavior when switching languages in polyglot services (different retry floors, TTL handling, and backoff jitter application). This PR harmonizes retry preset names and timebound semantics, adds telemetry-ready hooks for observability, and introduces a small ergonomic PullGenerator pull-based streaming facade (py/ts/go) to make async pull consumption more consistent across languages.

What this PR does (summary): Consolidate retry profile names to a canonical set (fast, balanced, durable), unify timebound semantics (max_attempt_time applies to whole operation, not per-attempt), surface retry lifecycle telemetry events (retry_attempt, retry_backoff_ms, retry_final), and add PullGenerator facade which wraps existing async iterators/streams and exposes a small synchronous/pull-oriented consumer API useful for server integrations. Also bumps SDK minor versions and updates examples, docs, and changelogs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-1912 design notes linked in the Linear ticket - [x] Cross-SDK tests: smoke, handshake and session replay tests - [x] Telemetry hooks implemented and documented - [x] Examples updated (py/ts/go) - [x] README/changelog entries added - [x] Version bumps and packaging metadata updated

Commits (high-level): - 8a2f3d4: unify retry preset enum and rename presets across sdks - 1b7c9d2: implement timebound max_attempt_time logic in python sdk - c4d12fa: add PullGenerator facade (typescript) and tests - e1b9a77: add PullGenerator facade (go) and session glue - f2c3b9a: add PullGenerator facade (python) and examples - d9e6b2a: add telemetry hooks and adapters across sdks - a7b5c4e: bump versions, update changelogs and readme snippets

Files/areas changed (high level): - sdk/python/redwood/transport/retry.py: consolidate profiles, implement operation-level max_attempt_time and telemetry hooks. Added PullGenerator wrapper in sdk/python/redwood/streaming/pull_generator.py. - sdk/typescript/src/retry/presets.ts: renamed presets and exported canonical enum; add telemetry emitter interface. - sdk/typescript/src/stream/pullGenerator.ts: new small facade that consumes existing async iterators and exposes pull responses. - sdk/go/retry/presets.go: align names and timebound semantics; introduce RetryTelemetry interface. - sdk/go/stream/pull_generator.go: new pull-oriented facade for io-like consumer patterns. - docs/sdk/retries.md: explain presets and timebound semantics. - examples/pull-generator/: three short examples (py/ts/go) showing server integration patterns. - CHANGELOGs: bumped per-sdk.

Illustrative snippet (typescript PullGenerator usage): const pg = new PullGenerator(chatStream); while (true) { const chunk = await pg.pull(); if (!chunk) break; processChunk(chunk); }

Review conversation (highlights): Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Nice to see a single source of truth for preset names. Question: can we keep the old names as aliases for one release cycle to avoid breaking downstream code that references presets by string?" Mira Chen (author): "Added alias map in TS and PY for one release cycle; Go preserves typed enum compatibility by adding deprecated constants. Documented aliases in RELEASES.md." Lena Ho (reviewer): "Telemetry looks good, but payload size from retry events could be noisy in high-throughput services. Can we make emission configurable with a minimal default?" Mira Chen: "Telemetry emitter defaults to no-op unless user opts into sdk telemetry or provides an emitter; added opt-in config flag 'enableRetryTelemetry' with default off." Raj Patel (reviewer): "PullGenerator API looks ergonomic. A nit: synchronous-style pull() returning Promise<null> on completion is a little odd for Go consumers. Consider returning (chunk, ok) tuple semantics in Go." Mira Chen: "Adjusted Go PullGenerator to return (chunk, ok, err) style and updated examples. Thanks for catching that."

Requested changes and follow-ups: - Added alias map and documented deprecated names. - Exposed nullable telemetry config with opt-in default off. - Adjusted Go pull semantics to idiomatic (value, ok, err). - Add perf microbenchmark for PullGenerator layer (follow-up ticket ENG-1978).

CI and testing: Initial CI run showed one flaky test in sdk/python/test_stream_resume::test_resume_after_reauth (transient websocket timing). I rebased and added a small backoff jitter in the test harness; rerun passed. Full matrix: python unit tests (pass), typescript unit + integration (pass), go unit tests (pass), linting (pass), packaging checks (pass). E2E cross-sdk smoke (mainnet-like) run passed locally and on CI.

Compatibility notes: No breaking API changes were introduced; all renamed presets have one-release aliases for backward compatibility. PullGenerator is additive and opt-in. Version bumps are patch/minor: python 1.12.2 -> 1.12.3, typescript 2.7.0 -> 2.7.1, go 0.9.7 -> 0.9.8.

Docs and examples: Added docs/sdk/retries.md describing canonical presets (fast, balanced, durable) and their recommended use-cases and cost/latency tradeoffs. Added docs/streaming/pull_generator.md with code examples in three languages and a short note on telemetry configuration. Updated changelogs with highlights and migration notes.

Migration guidance for customers: - If you reference retry presets by string, use alias names for one release; prefer the canonical enum values moving forward. - PullGenerator is optional; server-side frameworks that expect pull-based reads (e.g., synchronous web frameworks) can adopt it for simpler integration. - Telemetry hooks are opt-in and should be enabled only in dev/observability environments to avoid high-cardinality metrics.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-25 after approvals from Diego Ramos and Lena Ho and green CI. Release cuts scheduled by the release team: python/ts/go packages to be published within the next release window.

Post-merge follow-ups (open tasks): - ENG-1978: add microbenchmarks for PullGenerator overhead and confirm cost/latency numbers. - ENG-2009: add server-framework specific helper for fast server-side pull integration (express/fastapi/nethttp adapter). - Monitor telemetry opt-in adoption and adjust default if users request easier visibility.

If anything's unclear or you'd like a walk-through of the PullGenerator design (sync vs async tradeoffs) I'm happy to pair with reviewers to demo locally.
